To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the auditory system is able to provide online control of pointing movements directed toward an acoustic source.

the auditory-motor system is efficient in processing auditory information about the position of the hand in order to guide hand movements toward an auditory source, but that this system is not able to compensate for errors in target localization when the duration of target presentation is too short to allow the subject to process the auditory cues.
the auditory system is able to take advantages of dynamic changes in the acoustic cues due changes in the head orientation in order for online processing of the motor control of pointing movements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of the sensory-motor system in the production and control of movements.
the mechanisms whereby the auditory system contributes to the spatial control of motor activity.
the mechanisms of the auditory-movement coupling and the role of auditory feedback in motor control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
auditory feedback of hand movement can improve motor performance when the auditory feedback is informative and when the auditory feedback system is able to process this feedback online.
the auditory-motor system is an efficient and flexible system that allows the subject to control the trajectory of the pointing movement in the auditory space.

auditory information about hand movement position is not used to correct the trajectory of pointing movements to auditory targets, and that the auditory system is not able to process the information about hand position to correct movements directed at auditory targets in a continuous way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditory feedback is not a good predictor of the auditory feedback.
the human auditory-motor loop is an efficient and fast mechanism for online control and monitoring of pointing movements.
the human brain is able to process the information about the position of a target in space and to transform this information into a movement command.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auditory system is able to provide a reliable source of information to guide the motor system.
auditory information can be used as a feedback to control hand movements in a goal-directed reaching task.
the auditory system plays an important role in the control of movements toward auditory targets.
